To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FVIIA bound to EPCR activates PAR1-mediated signaling and protects the endothelial barrier.
FVII bound to EPCR activates PAR1 and mediates barrier protection.
factor VIIa bound to EPC receptor on endothelial cells protects against thrombin-induced disruption of the endothelial barrier by activating PAR1-mediated cell signal transduction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of factor VIIa (fVIIa) with its cellular receptor, endothelial cell protein c receptor (EPCR).
the molecular mechanisms by which factor VIIa, bound to EPCR, activates PAR1 and mediates endothelial cell signaling, barrier function, and vascular integrity.
the role of the endothelial cell in hemostasis and thrombosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FVII bound to EPCR protects endothelial barrier function via a novel signaling pathway involving activation of PAR1, Rac1 activation, and p44/42MAPK activation.
FVII bound to EPCR activates PAR1 and induces PAR1-dependent p44/42 ERK1/2 MAPK activation and barrier protection.
FVII bound to endothelial cells via EPCR activates PAR1 and induces cell signaling and provides barrier protection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

FVII/EPCR interaction on endothelial cells is not only a mechanism to regulate the anticoagulant function of the protein C pathway, but also a mechanism that regulates endothelial cell barrier function and vascular permeability.
FVII-EPCR interaction provides a barrier- protective effect and this effect may be beneficial in patients receiving FVIIa for the treatment of bleeding.
FVII bound to EPCR can protect endothelium against thrombin-induced damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FVII/EPCR/PAR1 axis plays a role in the protection of vascular barrier.
EPCR is a novel receptor for FVIIa that mediates PAR1 signaling and barrier protection.
FVII is not only a procoagulant factor, but also an anti-inflammatory factor.
